newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday January 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday January 21.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italy has requested a 600,000-tonne increase in its 9.9 million tonne annual EU milk quota. Italian farmers demonstrating against EU quotas partially lifted a four-day blockade of roads leading to Milan's main Linate airport after prime minister Romano Prodi promised to hear their grievances. A meeting is expected to take place on Wednesday afternoon.

* Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti warned the government against broader political alliances but softened its position on the sell-off of state telecoms giant STET and on government measures to boost the car market, which he had threatened to block. Deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said the ruling coalition should sign a six month truce with the hard-left Refoundation but added that privatisations will go ahead (all).
* The planned set-up of a bicameral commission to carry out constitutional reforms will be under examination from today in the lower house of parliament (all).

* Information technology group Olivetti announced the sale of its ailing personal computer business to newly constituted group Piedmont International in a deal worth 250 to 300 billion lire. A key role in the operation has been played by U.S. lawyer Edward Gottesman, chairman of Centenary group, one of the investors in Piedmont. Olivetti will retain a 10 percent stake in the new group.

* Italian January consumer prices are seen at a preliminary 2.5/2.6 percent year-on-year based on data released by two sample cities. A further nine cities will release their preliminary data today (all).
* Trade unions have asked to meet Prodi and employers' organisation Confindustria to rediscuss wage issues in the light of the long-running metalworkers' dispute (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi assured European Commissioner Karel Van Miert that the plan to transfer state telecom group STET to the Treasury will go ahead despite a negative parliament vote.
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
